summary: The speaker argues that memorable customer experiences hinge on deliberate bookends—the emotions customers feel at the start and at the end of an encounter. Using Griffin Hospital as a case study, she explains how a designed emotional journey transforms anxiety into calm through a set of concrete operational choices. By layering ambient cues (parking-lot music), practical services (valet, concierge), and family-friendly amenities (hot dog wagons for waiting children), the hospital aimed to reduce fear and foster a sense of partnership with families. The result, framed as formal action items, is a stronger brand story and faster growth, illustrating that emotion can be deliberately designed into service delivery—and tracked through outcomes and word-of-mouth narratives.
title: Deliberate Emotion Bookends: Designing Calm in Customer Experience (Griffin Hospital Case)
topics: fear and panic in hospital entry
